insight: The new Demon 170 engine underwent extensive revisions, including the replacement of significant components such as pistons, connecting rods, and billet main caps to handle the higher power output.
The 3.0-liter supercharger on the Demon 170 draws air through an enlarged throttle body and permits the fuel injectors to flow up to 164 gallons per hour, significantly boosting performance.
To manage the immense pressure from the 1,025 hp engine, Dodge replaced the cylinder-head bolts with stronger studs to enhance durability.
Engineers upgraded the crankshaft and crank bearings to prevent the new engine from self-destructing under the intense power load.
The Demon 170's fuel system was overhauled to support E85 fuel, which includes ethanol-resistant components and new spark plugs that optimize combustion.
The Demon 170 features an upgraded eight-speed automatic transmission and a hardened driveline to handle the vehicle's increased torque and horsepower.
The SRT Power Chiller technology uses the air conditioning system to lower the air induction temperature by up to 45°F, thus improving engine performance and reliability.
The engine block was fitted with billet-steel main caps, increasing clamping pressure by 44 percent to manage the higher internal cylinder pressures.
The fuel injectors were upgraded to accommodate the engine's requirements, capable of delivering 164 gallons per hour to secure the demanded performance.
A sophisticated torque-shaping technology was introduced to manage wheel spin and maintain traction, especially critical during drag launches.
